S.FORM: sua kisa-i canumu kisa-i=naku.
S.PHON: sua kisai ʦanumu kisainaku
S.FORM: sua kisai canumu kisainaku.
S.PHON: sua kisai ʦanumu kisainaku
S.TRANSL: I want to talk about water.

S.FORM: sua nimuruʔu ia, kaʔan taavalaʔə r<um>a-cəkəcə.
S.PHON: sua nimuruʔu ia kaʔan taavaɾaʔə rumaʦəkəʦə
S.FORM: sua nimuru'u ia, ka'an taavara'e r<um>acekece.
S.PHON: sua nimu[r|ɾ]uʔu ia kaʔan taava[r|ɾ]aʔe [r|ɾ]umaʦekeʦe
S.TRANSL: Blood must not be stepped on.

S.FORM: sua iisua ia, ʔuuna=kani ni-mu-ʔuna ʔinia maa-ʔunuŋ
S.PHON: sua iisua ia ʔuunakani nimuʔuna ʔinia maaʔunuŋ
S.FORM: sua iisua ia, 'uunakani nimu'una 'inia maa'unung
S.PHON: sua iisua ia ʔuunakani nimuʔuna ʔinia maaʔunuŋ
S.TRANSL: People were fighting there.

S.FORM: ma-naasə kanakanavu mata pakisia.
S.PHON: manaasə kanakanavu mata pakiʂia
S.FORM: manaase kanakanavu mata pakisia.
S.PHON: manaase kanakanavu mata pakiʂia
S.TRANSL: There were a Kanakanavu person and a Chinese person.

S.FORM: ni-mu-ʔuna=kani ʔinia paa-ra-ara-pici ʔu-rupaca=kani numan.
S.PHON: nimuʔunakani ʔinia paaraarapitʂi ʔurupaʦakani numan
S.FORM: nimu'unakani 'inia paaraarapici 'urupacakani numan.
S.PHON: nimuʔunakani ʔinia paa[r|ɾ]aa[r|ɾ]apitʂi ʔu[r|ɾ]upaʦakani numan
S.TRANSL: (The two) used machetes to slash at each other.

S.FORM: ma-kaasi=kani sua ni-varisiʔ-a, "m-icili-icili nimuruʔu ʔaisi ia, ʔakuni=ʔai r<əm>a-cəkəcə ʔinia."
S.PHON: makaaʂikani sua nivariʂiʔa mitʂiɾiitʂiɾi nimuruʔu ʔaiʂi ia ʔakuniʔai rəmaʦəkəʦə ʔinia
S.FORM: makaasikani sua nivarisi'a, "miciriiciri nimuru'u 'aisi ia, 'akuni'ai r<em>acekece 'inia."
S.PHON: makaaʂikani sua niva[r|ɾ]iʂiʔa mitʂi[r|ɾ]iitʂi[r|ɾ]i nimu[r|ɾ]uʔu ʔaiʂi ia ʔakuniʔai [r|ɾ]emaʦekeʦe ʔinia
S.TRANSL: The person who was cut said, "When blood is spilling, it must not be stepped on."

S.FORM: caniaava, nu ʔuuna cəkəcə=kani ʔinia ia, tia=aaka misai=kani.
S.PHON: ʦaniaava nu ʔuuna ʦəkəʦəkani ʔinia ia tiaaaka misaikani
S.FORM: caniaava, nu 'uuna cekecekani 'inia ia, tiaaaka misaikani.
S.PHON: ʦaniaava nu ʔuuna ʦekeʦekani ʔinia ia tiaaaka misaikani
S.TRANSL: For example, if someone steps on it, his foot will swell (lit., become bad).

S.FORM: r<əm>a-cəkə-cəkəcə=kamu ʔinia ia, tia=aaka misai=kani.
S.PHON: rəmaʦəkəʦəkəʦəkamu ʔinia ia tiaaaka misaikani
S.FORM: r<em>acekecekecekamu 'inia ia, tiaaaka misaikani.
S.PHON: [r|ɾ]emaʦekeʦekeʦekamu ʔinia ia tiaaaka misaikani
S.TRANSL: If you step on it, (your feet) will swell (lit., become bad).

S.FORM: kaʔan=pi=kia aa-manəŋ si nimuruʔu=kara pakisia si nimuruʔu=kara kanakanavu. kaʔan=pi=kia taavalaʔə.
S.PHON: kaʔanpikia aamanəŋ ʂi nimuruʔukara pakiʂia ʂi nimuruʔukara kanakanavu kaʔanpikia taavaɾaʔə
S.FORM: ka'anpikia aamaneng si nimuru'ukara pakisia si nimuru'ukara kanakanavu. ka'anpikia taavara'e.
S.PHON: kaʔanpikia aamaneŋ ʂi nimu[r|ɾ]uʔuka[r|ɾ]a pakiʂia ʂi nimu[r|ɾ]uʔuka[r|ɾ]a kanakanavu kaʔanpikia taava[r|ɾ]aʔe
S.TRANSL: It's not clear to me if it is because of the Chinese blood or the Kanakanavu blood. I don't know yet.

S.FORM: taavalaʔə=ku canumu iisua, ta-ʔuici maamia ma-caasə.
S.PHON: taavaɾaʔəku ʦanumu iisua taʔuitʂi maamia maʦaasə
S.FORM: taavara'eku canumu iisua, ta'uici maamia macaase.
S.PHON: taava[r|ɾ]aʔeku ʦanumu iisua taʔuitʂi maamia maʦaase
S.TRANSL: I know that water, and (the flowing water with blood) is tiny and long.

S.FORM: maica=kia ʔinia ia, masi-vaʔatə=kia caən masi-tərəkə pita-kusa ʔinia.
S.PHON: maiʦakia ʔinia ia maʂivaʔatəkia ʦaən maʂitərəkə pitakusa ʔinia
S.FORM: maicakia 'inia ia, masiva'atekia caen masitereke pitakusa 'inia.
S.PHON: maiʦakia ʔinia ia maʂivaʔatekia ʦaen maʂite[r|ɾ]eke pitakusa ʔinia
S.TRANSL: When I was passing there, I would pull up some grass, tear off (branches with leaves) and throw them over there (so that I could step on them).

S.FORM: taavalaʔə miciko=maku.
S.PHON: taavaɾaʔə mitʂikomaku
S.FORM: taavara'e micikomaku.
S.PHON: taava[r|ɾ]aʔe mitʂikomaku
S.TRANSL: My wife Michiko also knows it.

S.FORM: maica=kia ʔinia ia, masi-vaʔatə=kia caən pita-kusa ʔinia.
S.PHON: maiʦakia ʔinia ia maʂivaʔatəkia ʦaən pitakusa ʔinia
S.FORM: maicakia 'inia ia, masiva'atekia caen pitakusa 'inia.
S.PHON: maiʦakia ʔinia ia maʂivaʔatekia ʦaen pitakusa ʔinia
S.TRANSL: When I was passing there, I would pull up some grass and throw it over there (so that I could step on them).

S.FORM: nuu kaa pita-kusa ʔinia caən ia, kaʔan taavalaʔə r<um>a-cəkəcə.
S.PHON: nuu kaa pitakusa ʔinia ʦaən ia kaʔan taavaɾaʔə rumaʦəkəʦə
S.FORM: nuu kaa pitakusa 'inia caen ia, ka'an taavara'e r<um>acekece.
S.PHON: nuu kaa pitakusa ʔinia ʦaen ia kaʔan taava[r|ɾ]aʔe [r|ɾ]umaʦekeʦe
S.TRANSL: If you don't throw some grass over there, you can't step on it.

S.FORM: ara-aka=kani ʔacipi.
S.PHON: araakakani ʔatʂipi
S.FORM: araakakani 'acipi.
S.PHON: a[r|ɾ]aakakani ʔatʂipi
S.TRANSL: The foot will become swollen (lit., become bad).

S.FORM: maka-sua sua t<in>mana=maku kaari miana nakai sua kaari iisi ia, cu-culu.
S.PHON: makasua sua tinmanamaku kaari miana nakai sua kaari iiʂi ia ʦuʦuɾu
S.FORM: makasua sua t<in>manamaku kaari miana nakai sua kaari iisi ia, cucuru.
S.PHON: makasua sua tinmanamaku kaa[r|ɾ]i miana nakai sua kaa[r|ɾ]i iiʂi ia ʦuʦu[r|ɾ]u
S.TRANSL: This is what I heard from the past, but it is true.

S.FORM: ni-m-ari-avici=cu=ku gookoosho mu-kusa ʔinia.
S.PHON: nimariavitʂiʦuku *ookoosho mukusa ʔinia
S.FORM: nimariavicicuku gookoosho mukusa 'inia.
S.PHON: nima[r|ɾ]iavitʂiʦuku *ookoosho mukusa ʔinia
S.TRANSL: I once took an officer from a city district there.

S.FORM: ni-mu-kusa=cu ʔinia gookoosho naatia paa-tara-ʔaniŋu, nakai ʔakia=cu ʔinia vaatu.
S.PHON: nimukusaʦu ʔinia *ookoosho naatia paataraʔaniŋu nakai ʔakiaʦu ʔinia vaatu
S.FORM: nimukusacu 'inia gookoosho naatia paatara'aningu, nakai 'akiacu 'inia vaatu.
S.PHON: nimukusaʦu ʔinia *ookoosho naatia paata[r|ɾ]aʔaniŋu nakai ʔakiaʦu ʔinia vaatu
S.TRANSL: The officer went there to take some photographs, but there were no rocks.

S.FORM: ni-i-vaʔatə mia su-raru-in.
S.PHON: niivaʔatə mia suraruin
S.FORM: niiva'ate mia suraruin.
S.PHON: niivaʔate mia su[r|ɾ]a[r|ɾ]uin
S.TRANSL: They were carried away by a storm in passing.

S.FORM: mia t<um>aparu-in su-raru ia, manaasə ni-i-vaʔatə=kiai vaatu mia-iisua.
S.PHON: mia tumaparuin suraru ia manaasə niivaʔatəkiai vaatu miaiisua
S.FORM: mia t<um>aparuin suraru ia, manaase niiva'atekiai vaatu miaiisua.
S.PHON: mia tumapa[r|ɾ]uin su[r|ɾ]a[r|ɾ]u ia manaase niivaʔatekiai vaatu miaiisua
S.TRANSL: When the terrifying storm came, (we) were swept away by a mudslide.

S.FORM: a-piaica=pa maamia sian kari=maku.
S.PHON: apiaiʦapa maamia ʂian karimaku
S.FORM: apiaicapa maamia sian karimaku.
S.PHON: apiaiʦapa maamia ʂian ka[r|ɾ]imaku
S.TRANSL: I will end here with my words.

S.FORM: sua iikamu ma-manu taa-tiʔiŋ ia, tee=pa tara-vəavəa ia, tee=pa pita-cəkəna ia, ari-ʔiari-ana t<un>mana manasi taavalaʔə=kamu kaari iisua.
S.PHON: sua iikamu mamanu taatiʔiŋ ia teepa taravəavəa ia teepa pitaʦəkəna ia ariʔiariana tunmana manaʂi taavaɾaʔəkamu kaari iisua
S.FORM: sua iikamu mamanu taati'ing ia, teepa taraveavea ia, teepa pitacekena ia, ari'iariana t<un>mana manasi taavara'ekamu kaari iisua.
S.PHON: sua iikamu mamanu taatiʔiŋ ia teepa ta[r|ɾ]aveavea ia teepa pitaʦekena ia a[r|ɾ]iʔia[r|ɾ]iana tunmana manaʂi taava[r|ɾ]aʔekamu kaa[r|ɾ]i iisua
S.TRANSL: Young people like you who are still alive, and if you still have the time you may take your time (considering) the words you hear, and you will understand them.

S.FORM: "maka-sua kaari ma-maaraŋ miana misai=kamu. taavalaʔə=pi=kia pu-kari-kari si ʔeesi=pi=kia t<in>puru sua iiku ia," cuma muʔu kisa-ən. "taavalaʔə=pa=ku əkər-au=pa=ku=ʔai." maamanai.
S.PHON: makasua kaari mamaaraŋ miana misaikamu taavaɾaʔəpikia pukarikari ʂi ʔeeʂipikia tinpuru sua iiku ia ʦuma muʔu kisaən taavaɾaʔəpaku əkəraupakuʔai maamanai
S.FORM: "makasua kaari mamaarang miana misaikamu. taavara'epikia pukarikari si 'eesipikia t<in>puru sua iiku ia," cuma mu'u kisaen. "taavara'epaku ekeraupaku'ai." maamanai.
S.PHON: makasua kaa[r|ɾ]i mamaa[r|ɾ]aŋ miana misaikamu taava[r|ɾ]aʔepikia puka[r|ɾ]ika[r|ɾ]i ʂi ʔeeʂipikia tinpu[r|ɾ]u sua iiku ia ʦuma muʔu kisaen taava[r|ɾ]aʔepaku eke[r|ɾ]aupakuʔai maamanai
S.TRANSL: "The words I'm telling you are (what I heard) from the past. I can still talk when I am still sitting around," Uncle Mu'u said, "I hope I can still hold onto these words in the world."

S.FORM: ara-siŋsiŋ-a.
S.PHON: araʂiŋʂiŋa
S.FORM: arasingsinga.
S.PHON: a[r|ɾ]aʂiŋʂiŋa
S.TRANSL: Stay healthy!
